labelChirho: be narrow, be in distress (Qal stative)
descriptionChirho: Qal stative/intransitive sense: to be narrow, tight, or in distress — the basic condition of being constricted or troubled, evidenced by multilingual glosses like 'distress/angustia/संकट/ضيق' and 'too narrow/estrecha/तंग/좁다'.

Qal active/transitive sense: to bind, wrap up, or tie — the physical act of binding or wrapping something, evidenced by glosses like 'has wrapped/envolvió/बाँध लिया' and 'binding-up/atando/बाँधने वाला', including the imperative 'bind up' and the infinitive 'like binding'.

Qal passive participle sense: to be bound, shut up, or confined — the resultant state of having been bound or enclosed, evidenced by multilingual glosses like 'shut-up/encerradas/बंदी/محبوسات' and 'is-bound-up/atado/बांधा हुआ/مصرور'.

Hifil causative sense: to cause distress, bring trouble upon, or besiege — the causative of the stative 'be in distress', evidenced by glosses like 'I will cause distress/angustiaré/तंग करूँगा' and 'besieges/angustiará/घेरे/ضايق'.

Pual passive-intensive sense: to be patched or mended — a specialized usage of the binding root in the intensive-passive stem, evidenced by glosses like 'patched/remendados/बंधी हुई/مرقّعة', referring to wineskins in Joshua 9:4.
